# Duplicate content

There is no duplicate content penalty: Google's documentation says some duplicate content is normal and not a spam-policy violation, and Day 2 described deduplication as clustering duplicates, indexing one representative URL and forwarding the signals of every URL in the cluster, such as links, to it. Google deduplicates because users do not want repeated results and the index has no room for everything; on stage it added rising storage costs, which is not in its docs. Clusters are built from redirects, content, rel=canonical and other inputs, and Google said content clustering catches exact matches, near matches such as pages with a translated template but untranslated main content, soft 404s and URL patterns, which can fold city or service pages into one canonical without each page being looked at (the four-way split and the pattern behaviour are not in Google's docs). A CDN challenge page served with a 200 status on many URLs can get them clustered as well, and Google's troubleshooting guide says pages split out once they are clearly different, which can take up to two weeks after a fix. Author's view: the real costs are losing control over which URL is chosen and crawling spent on copies. Day 3 widened the frame: Google's spam slide said sites with mostly scraped content and no added services or content may not provide value to users, and a community speaker said some keyword cannibalization is logical and fine, while for harmful cases the agency groups an article's Search Console queries before deciding whether to redirect the pages or rewrite and split the content. The second recording of Day 1 added the basics: Google clusters duplicates and picks one representative, the canonical, so users are not shown duplicates, and when a page is selected for the index its whole duplicate cluster goes in with it. A community speaker treated similar URLs (protocol, host, case, slashes, encoding, parameter order) as an indicator of duplicate content, and in the Q&A Google suggested redirecting parameter variants to the normalised URL; another community speaker advised against markdown copies of pages for AI agents, a duplicate (which the speaker also called a possible source of cloaking, a word the recordings disagree on). Day 2's second recording completed the deduplication talk: in a migration the site owner says the old and new domains are the same and that Google should pick the new one, and the short advice for same-language, different-country pages was to use hreflang. A Day 2 case study merged two competing loan-comparison sites and folded pages with the same search intent into one strong article each, from over 2,000 URLs to about 100.

Based on: `D1-C111`, `D1-C112`, `D1-C128`, `D2-C345`, `D2-C348`, `D2-C349`, `D2-C344`, `D2-C350`, `D2-C360`, `D2-C364`, `D2-C366`, `D2-C367`, `D2-C368`, `D2-C370`, `D2-C374`, `D2-C376`, `D2-C373`, `D1-C113`, `D2-C390`, `D2-C399`, `D2-C396`, `D2-C371`, `D2-C372`, `D2-C382`, `D2-C384`, `D2-C450`, `D2-C451`, `D3-C280`, `D3-C489`, `D1-C207`, `D1-C212`, `D1-C397`, `D1-C399`, `D1-C445`, `D1-C272`, `D2-C351`, `D2-C874`, `D2-C881`.

## What to do

- Signal the preferred URL consistently with redirects, rel=canonical, internal links and sitemaps.
- Make location, variant and country pages differ in their main content, and return 404 for empty or invalid combinations, so URL patterns are not folded into one canonical.
- Serve bot challenges to crawlers with a 503 status, never as a 200 page.
- Use hreflang with region codes for same-language country versions, such as de-DE, de-AT and de-CH.
- Put the same structured data on duplicates as on the canonical.
- After fixing a wrong cluster, allow up to two weeks before judging the result.

- **[Stage]** The first reason Google deduplicates is that users do not want to see the same page repeated in the search results, even if site owners would like it to rank ten times on page one.
  <br><sub>`D2-C349` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization), [A guide to Google Search ranking systems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ranking-systems-guide)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Storage is a second reason for deduplication: Google's storage has many competing uses and storage prices have risen sharply, so the space for any one use is limited and Google has to draw a line somewhere.
  <br><sub>`D2-C350` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google treats a site migration as deduplication across sites, in which the site owner says the old and the new domain are the same and that Google should pick the new domain, so deduplication also helps Google handle migrations.

- **[Slide]** Google keeps the other URLs of a duplicate cluster as 'alternate names': equivalent URLs with the same content that Google still tracks as alternate versions of the representative URL.

- **[Slide]** Alternate names also serve localization: if Google knows that country versions such as you.de and you.at are equivalent, it can pick the right version to show using hreflang.
  <br><sub>`D2-C353` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Alternate names are why a site: query for an old domain still shows the old domain's URLs after a site migration, which site owners often misread as a migration that is not working.
  > "FYI "alternate names" is why you see old domains in site:-queries"

- **[Stage]** Google's duplication talk described three related parts of deduplication: building clusters, localization, and selecting the representative URL, which is the canonicalization site owners see in Search Console.

- **[Stage]** Google builds duplicate clusters from four kinds of input: redirects, content, rel=canonical, and a 'magic bucket' of other things.
  <br><sub>`D2-C360` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google trusts redirects very much for clustering, because a redirect is a clear sign that there is one version of the content; Google keeps track of both URLs but stores only one copy of the content.
  <br><sub>`D2-C361` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Redirects and Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects), [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Used by `DEV-CAN-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Whether a redirect is permanent or temporary matters only for choosing the canonical, not for clustering the URLs together.
  > "the permanent redirect really only matters for canonicalization, not for clustering."
  <br><sub>`D2-C362` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Redirects and Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects) · Used by `DEV-CAN-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google clusters duplicate pages by content in four ways: exact matches, near matches, structurally similar content, and soft 404s.
  <br><sub>`D2-C364` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Exact-match duplicates, such as the www and non-www versions of the same page, are clustered and Google keeps only one of them.
  <br><sub>`D2-C365` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) · Used by `DEV-CAN-02`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Pages whose boilerplate, such as menu and footer, is translated while the main content is not are near matches: the main reason to visit is the same, so Google clusters them as duplicates.
  > "When main content is the same, pages may be clustered."
  <br><sub>`D2-C366` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization), [Tell Google about localized versions of your page](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/localized-versions) · Used by `DEV-INT-07`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Soft 404 pages are another reason Google clusters pages together, an outcome site owners usually do not want.
  <br><sub>`D2-C367` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Fix canonicalization issues](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting), [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns) · Extends [D1-C073](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Used by `DEV-ERR-01`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google sometimes picks a canonical that looks unrelated because it recognised a URL pattern: if /buy/fax, /buy/typewriter and /office-equipment show the same content, its systems may assume any /buy/ URL, even /buy/seo-service, shows that same office-equipment content without looking at the page.
  <br><sub>`D2-C368` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-CAN-08`, `DEV-URL-09`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's slide on structurally similar content asked whether a new URL that fits a known duplicate pattern, such as /buy/seo-service, even needs to be crawled.
  > "Do we even need to crawl /buy/seo-service ?"
  <br><sub>`D2-C369` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · not in Google docs · Extends [D1-C128](../sessions/D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Extends [D1-C094](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) · Used by `DEV-CAN-08`, `DEV-URL-09`</sub>

- **[Slide]** City pages can trigger the same pattern-based deduplication: for a car dealer brand with branches in several cities and similar stock, Google's systems may decide the city name does not matter and canonicalise to one city's page; the slide asked whether a further city page such as /zurich/services would be treated the same way.
  <br><sub>`D2-C370` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-CAN-08`</sub>

- **[Slide]** To avoid pattern-based deduplication, Google's speaker recommended not having many unrelated, similar-looking URLs that lead to the same content, and returning error pages for URLs that no longer exist so they are clearly unrelated.
  > "Misleading site structure (use clear signals!)"
  <br><sub>`D2-C371` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Fix canonicalization issues](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting), [Troubleshoot Google Search crawling errors](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/troubleshoot-crawling-errors) · Used by `DEV-CAN-08`, `DEV-URL-09`</sub>

- **[Stage]** A growing cause of wrong clustering is bot protection: when a CDN or another protection system shows Googlebot the same 'you look like a bot, solve this puzzle' page on many unrelated URLs or domains, Google can cluster those pages as duplicates.
  <br><sub>`D2-C374` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns), [Fix canonicalization issues](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting) · Extends [D1-C069](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Extends [D1-C078](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Extends [D1-C367](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Used by `DEV-SRV-01`, `DEV-SRV-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's systems find it very hard to recognise a bot-challenge page as an error page, and Googlebot cannot solve the puzzles, such as selecting all the cats, that those pages ask for.
  <br><sub>`D2-C375` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns) · Extends [D1-C367](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Used by `DEV-SRV-01`, `DEV-SRV-02`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Same-language content for different countries is tricky for Google's deduplication, notably German pages for Germany, Austria and Switzerland, and possibly Spanish-language variants.
  <br><sub>`D2-C381` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization), [Managing multi-regional and multilingual sites](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/managing-multi-regional-sites) · Used by `DEV-INT-08`</sub>

- **[Slide]** When localized pages are clustered, Google tries to use hreflang alternates; the speaker's short version of the advice was to use hreflang, which he called really helpful for same-language, different-country content.
  > "We try to use hreflang alternates."
  <br><sub>`D2-C382` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization), [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Extends [D2-C033](../sessions/D2-S03-how-is-html-interpreted.md) · Used by `DEV-INT-08`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's speaker advised against 'clever' geo-redirecting, because it very often goes wrong.
  > "clever" geo-redirecting (is often not so clever)"
  <br><sub>`D2-C383` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · confirmed by Google docs · [Managing multi-regional and multilingual sites](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/managing-multi-regional-sites) · Used by `DEV-INT-02`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google watches for canonical hijacking, where several domains try to be canonical for the same content, whether accidentally across a site owner's own domains (such as a staging copy) or through third-party domains, maliciously or not, and asks site owners to report cases it gets wrong.
  <br><sub>`D2-C388` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [Fix canonicalization issues](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting), [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) · Used by `DEV-CAN-07`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's closing suggestions on duplication: use redirects for site migrations, use HTTP result codes, don't block agents, check your rel=canonical links, use hreflang links to help Google localize, report weird canonicals in the forums, make secure pages that work, and keep canonical signals clear.
  <br><sub>`D2-C396` · Day 2, Handling web duplication (John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead) · consistent with Google docs · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls), [How to move a site](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes), [Tell Google about localized versions of your page](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/localized-versions), [Troubleshoot Google Search crawling errors](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/troubleshoot-crawling-errors) · Extended by [D2-C882](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) · Used by `DEV-CAN-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** In a community speaker's terms, a canonical group is the set of all URLs connected through canonical links, and its canonical leader is the page that all the group's canonical links ultimately point to.
  <br><sub>`D2-C407` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker advised auditing canonicals as whole canonical groups rather than pair by pair, paying special attention to each group's canonical leader.
  <br><sub>`D2-C408` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Tobias Schwarz) · Extends [D1-C128](../sessions/D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Extends [D2-C398](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Used by `DEV-MON-06`</sub>

- **[Stage]** In a community case study, two of the first loan-comparison websites in Poland did exactly the same thing, so they competed with each other for the same users, the same keywords and the same space in search results.
  <br><sub>`D2-C874` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Martyna Ağanoğlu)</sub>

- **[Stage]** In a community case study, the kept pages that shared the same search intent were merged into one strong article each, taking the merged site from over 2,000 URLs to about 100, a cut of about 95% of URLs.
  <br><sub>`D2-C881` · Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves (Martyna Ağanoğlu)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google runs deduplication before feature extraction, so that the expensive extraction work is spent only on a trimmed-down, manageable set of documents.
  <br><sub>`D2-C444` · Day 2, Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more! (Gary Illyes) · not in Google docs · Extends [D2-C026](../sessions/D2-S03-how-is-html-interpreted.md) · Used by `DEV-SDA-10`</sub>

- **[Stage]** When Google already has duplicate information for a document, for example when reprocessing it, index selection uses it to drop non-canonical duplicates from further processing, so that, as the speaker put it, only canonicals end up in search results (a simplification; see D2-C703).
  <br><sub>`D2-C701` · Day 2, Deciding what goes in the index? (Google) · consistent with Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization), [Page indexing report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7440203?hl=en) · Extends [D1-C128](../sessions/D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Extends [D2-C345](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's slide said sites with mostly scraped content, taken from other sites without additional useful services or content, may not provide added value to users.
  <br><sub>`D3-C280` · Day 3, What are quality updates (Google) · consistent with Google docs · [Spam policies for Google web search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Nik Vujic said some keyword cannibalization is fine because it is logical, but for bad cannibalization his agency groups all of an article's Search Console queries and then decides whether to redirect the pages or rewrite and split the content.
  <br><sub>`D3-C489` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (Nik Vujic)</sub>

## What Google's documentation says

- **[Docs]** Google's canonicalization guide says some duplicate content on a site is normal and not a violation of its spam policies; Google clusters duplicate pages, picks the most representative one as canonical and crawls the duplicates less often.
  > "Some duplicate content on a site is normal and it's not a violation of Google's spam policies."
  <br><sub>`D1-C128` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 1, session not recorded · is the documentation · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) · Repeated by [D1-C207](../sessions/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Extended by [D2-C031](../sessions/D2-S03-how-is-html-interpreted.md) · Extended by [D2-C345](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Extended by [D2-C369](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Extended by [D2-C408](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) · Extended by [D2-C701](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) · Used by the glossary term *Duplicate cluster*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's canonicalization guide says that when Google indexes a page it determines the page's primary content, which it also calls the centerpiece, and clusters pages whose primary content is the same or very similar.
  > "When Google indexes a page, it determines the primary content (or centerpiece) of each page."
  <br><sub>`D2-C310` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Understanding what's on a page · is the documentation · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) · Used by `DEV-HTM-01`, the glossary term *Main content (centerpiece)*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's redirects guide says Google keeps track of both the source and the target of a redirect: one becomes the canonical, depending on signals such as whether the redirect is permanent or temporary, and the other becomes an alternate name that may appear in results when a query suggests the user trusts the old URL more. After a move to a new domain, old URLs may still show occasionally; the guide calls this normal.
  > "This is normal and as users get used to the new domain name, the alternate names will fade away without you doing anything."
  <br><sub>`D2-C357` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · is the documentation · [Redirects and Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects) · Used by `DEV-CAN-01`, `DEV-CAN-09`, the glossary term *Alternate names*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's canonicalization troubleshooting guide says fixing a wrong duplicate cluster comes down to making the clustered pages sufficiently different; pages split out faster when the difference is clear and significant, and Google may keep pages in a duplicate cluster for up to two weeks after a fix.
  <br><sub>`D2-C373` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · is the documentation · [Fix canonicalization issues](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting) · Used by `DEV-CAN-08`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Search Central post on CDNs says that if Google cannot recognise an error message served with a 200 status as an error, all pages showing the same message may be dropped from the index as duplicates, and recovery can be slow because Google has little incentive to recrawl duplicates. For bot-verification interstitials it recommends sending crawlers a 503 status.
  <br><sub>`D2-C376` · Search Central blog (24 December 2024) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · is the documentation · [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns) · Extends [D1-C078](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Used by `DEV-ERR-03`, `DEV-SRV-02`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's guide to specifying canonical URLs says a canonical helps consolidate signals for duplicate pages: links to a duplicate URL are consolidated with links to the preferred URL once the preferred URL becomes canonical.
  <br><sub>`D2-C430` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · is the documentation · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Used by `DEV-CAN-05`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's general structured data guidelines recommend placing the same structured data on all duplicate pages of the same content, not just on the canonical page.
  > "we recommend placing the same structured data on all page duplicates, not just on the canonical page"
  <br><sub>`D2-C451` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more! · is the documentation · [General structured data guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/sd-policies) · Used by `DEV-SDA-10`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's documentation says a search result usually points to the canonical page, but the other pages in a duplicate cluster are alternate versions that may be served in different contexts, for example a mobile page for a user on a mobile device.
  <br><sub>`D2-C702` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Deciding what goes in the index? · is the documentation · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization), [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works)</sub>

## What the press reported

- **[Press]** As reported by Search Engine Journal, John Mueller said in April 2026 that there is no penalty or ranking demotion for having multiple URLs with the same content; Google picks one to keep.
  > "There's no penalty or ranking demotion if you have multiple URLs going to the same content."
  <br><sub>`D1-C112` · Search Engine Journal (8 April 2026) · annotates Day 1, session not recorded · is the press report · [Google Says It Can Handle Multiple URLs To The Same Content](https://www.searchenginejournal.com/google-says-it-can-handle-multiple-urls-to-the-same-content/571424/)</sub>

## Analysis

- **[Analysis]** The real cost of duplicates is control and crawling: Google may choose a canonical you did not want, and every copy is still crawled. Copied or scraped content is a separate spam-policy issue.
  <br><sub>`D1-C113` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 1, session not recorded · Extended by [D2-C380](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Extended by [D2-C401](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Make location and variant pages differ in their main content (local stock, staff, prices, addresses) and return 404 for empty or invalid combinations; otherwise every URL that fits the pattern can be folded into one canonical.
  <br><sub>`D2-C372` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · Used by `DEV-CAN-08`, `DEV-URL-09`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For German-language sites serving Germany, Austria and Switzerland, add hreflang with region codes (de-DE, de-AT, de-CH) and make the country pages differ in more than boilerplate (prices, shipping, legal details), or expect Google to cluster them and show one.
  <br><sub>`D2-C384` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · Used by `DEV-INT-08`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Because Google extracts structured data, images and videos only after deduplication, put markup and media on the URL you want as canonical and keep them identical on its duplicates; markup that exists only on a duplicate that loses canonical selection may never be extracted.
  <br><sub>`D2-C450` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more! · Used by `DEV-SDA-10`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** 'Only canonicals end up in search results' as said on stage is a simplification: non-canonical duplicates are dropped from the index, but Google's documentation says an alternate from the same cluster can still be shown in some contexts, such as a mobile version to a mobile user.
  <br><sub>`D2-C703` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Deciding what goes in the index?</sub>

## Built on these claims

The items of the developer and content kits that rest on this topic's claims.

- Requirement `DEV-AIF-02`: Spend no effort on llms.txt, AI text files or AI-specific markup for Google
- Requirement `DEV-CAN-01`: Use permanent server-side redirects (301 or 308) for moved URLs, straight to the final URL
- Requirement `DEV-CAN-02`: Serve one host over HTTPS with a valid certificate and redirect every other origin to it
- Requirement `DEV-CAN-03`: Put exactly one absolute rel=canonical in the server-rendered head of every indexable page
- Requirement `DEV-CAN-05`: Make all canonical signals agree: redirects, rel=canonical, internal links, sitemaps and hreflang
- Requirement `DEV-CAN-07`: Never leave staging, preview or mirror copies of the site publicly crawlable
- Requirement `DEV-CAN-08`: Make pages that share a URL pattern differ in their main content
- Requirement `DEV-CAN-09`: Keep migration redirects in place long term and judge a move in Search Console, not with site: queries
- Requirement `DEV-CAN-10`: Redirect an old URL only to a page with the same intent, and return 404 or 410 when there is none
- Requirement `DEV-ERR-01`: Return 404 or 410 for removed and non-existent URLs
- Requirement `DEV-ERR-03`: Never serve error states, empty results or failed data loads with a 200 status
- Requirement `DEV-HTM-01`: Wrap each page's primary content in one clearly delimited main area
- Requirement `DEV-INT-02`: Do not redirect visitors automatically by IP address or browser language
- Requirement `DEV-INT-07`: Make each page's language unambiguous by translating the template with the main content
- Requirement `DEV-INT-08`: Differentiate same-language country versions beyond boilerplate and mark them with region codes
- Requirement `DEV-MON-06`: Audit canonical groups with a crawler on a schedule
- Requirement `DEV-SDA-10`: Put the same structured data on duplicate URLs as on the canonical
- Requirement `DEV-SRV-01`: Let verified Google crawlers through firewalls, CDNs and bot protection
- Requirement `DEV-SRV-02`: Never serve bot challenges or error pages to crawlers with a 200 status
- Requirement `DEV-URL-09`: If facet URLs must be crawlable, use & separators, a fixed filter order and 404 for empty results
- Requirement `DEV-URL-11`: Compute the expected URL for every request and redirect variants to it
- Glossary term *Alternate names*
- Glossary term *Canonical*
- Glossary term *Duplicate cluster*
- Glossary term *Main content (centerpiece)*
- Glossary term *Similar URLs*
